title: Oscar and the Summit
premise: Ada Nystrom, a desert ranger with a stolen compass and a debt she can't name, is hired to track a thief who vanished upriver into the Karst Reach. When the expedition's radio goes silent, Ada and her reluctant guide, the thief himself, discover a mining consortium has seized the high valley and silenced everyone who saw its illegal claims. Trapped by the monsoon with a leaking boat, they must survive on a stranger's help and reach the glacier pass before calving season closes it. In the end, Ada chooses justice outside the law—exposing the consortium by carrying their ledger downriver herself—and lets the thief go, paying her debt to the dead instead of to the company.
about_author: Freya Sandoval is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons running freight through monsoon country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who owe more than they can carry.

chapters.title: The Weight of Nothing
chapters.summary: Ada Nystrom tracks a thief across the salt flats, POV hers, establishing her competence, her broken compass, and the unnamed debt that drives her. Emotional beat: lonely resolve.

chapters.title: A Debt in Salt
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter in Ada's POV revealing the debt: her brother's death tied to a company contract she signed. She accepts a bounty job from the Meridian Consortium. Beat: guilt weaponized.

chapters.title: The Thief at the Well
chapters.summary: Ada corners the thief, Ilya Voss, at a desert well; he talks instead of runs, claiming he stole not money but a ledger. Beat: first spark of doubt.

chapters.title: Hired Hands
chapters.summary: Consortium agents arrive to take Ilya 'for processing.' Ada, paid to deliver him alive, watches them nearly kill him. Beat: the law she serves shows its teeth.

chapters.title: Upriver Contract
chapters.summary: Ada renegotiates: she'll escort Ilya upriver to the expedition station herself, where an independent survey team can verify the ledger. Beat: cautious alliance.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: POV alternates as they buy passage on a rotting riverboat captained by Sefa, a laconic stranger with her own reasons for avoiding checkpoints. Beat: uneasy truce on water.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: First storm hits; Ada and Ilya bail water together through the night while Sefa navigates blind. Beat: forced intimacy, grudging respect.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Kell's Landing
chapters.summary: A Consortium checkpoint demands papers they don't have; Sefa bribes, Ada bluffs, Ilya hides in the bilge. Beat: Ada realizes she's now the criminal.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: They reach the survey station and find it ransacked, radio smashed, one survivor delirious, whispering about 'the valley that eats names.' Beat: dread.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ilya finally opens the ledger: the Consortium has been buying deaths—claim-jumping via 'accidents'—including, Ada sees, the crew of her brother's last run. Beat: grief detonates.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals her sister was one of those 'accidents'; she'll take them upriver to the mining camp but wants the ledger destroyed after. Beat: three wounds, one direction.

chapters.title: The Valley That Eats Names
chapters.summary: Journey deeper: drowned villages, bought-off officials, a landscape erased from maps. Beat: scale of corruption becomes real.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Consortium gunboats trap them in the narrows; Sefa runs the rapids, boat holed below the waterline. Beat: adrenaline, near-death, trust forged.

chapters.title: Stranger's Help
chapters.summary: Wrecked, they're pulled from the river by Toma, an old hermit ferryman who owes Ilya's father a life-debt. Beat: unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Mending What Leaks
chapters.summary: Days repairing the boat in Toma's cove; Ada teaches Ilya to read current, he teaches her to rest. Beat: love begins, unspoken.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Holds
chapters.summary: Storms pin them down; supplies dwindle; Ada and Ilya argue over whether to turn back or push on. Beat: duty versus desire made explicit.

chapters.title: Toma's Story
chapters.summary: Toma recounts the massacre at the high valley twenty years ago—the same pattern, the same company under another name. Beat: history rhymes; stakes widen.

chapters.title: Patrol
chapters.summary: A Consortium patrol sweeps the cove; Toma covers for them at terrible cost, his ferry burned. Beat: guilt deepens; no going back.

chapters.title: The Glacier Road
chapters.summary: Toma tells them the only route past the camp opens when the glacier calves—a two-day window each season, days away. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Confession in the Bilge
chapters.summary: Ilya admits he didn't steal the ledger—he was the Consortium's auditor who defected after signing off on the 'accidents.' Beat: betrayal and forgiveness entangled.

chapters.title: Ada's Choice
chapters.summary: Ada confronts her own complicity: her brother died on a run she booked. She decides the debt is owed to the dead, not the employer. Beat: moral pivot.

chapters.title: Kiss Against the Storm
chapters.summary: On the eve of the attempt, Ada and Ilya acknowledge what they feel and agree it may cost everything. Beat: love against duty, tender and doomed-feeling.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: The glacier calves with thunder; the pass opens. They launch through ice-choked water as the window begins closing. Beat: awe and terror.

chapters.title: The Mining Camp
chapters.summary: They infiltrate the camp posing as contractors; Ada sees the machinery of erasure—bribed magistrates, falsified manifests. Beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Ada meets Director Hale, who offers her everything: her debt cleared, her record wiped, if she delivers Ilya and burns the ledger. Beat: temptation at full strength.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Ada pretends to accept, buying time; Ilya, unaware, feels betrayed all over again. Beat: dramatic irony tightens the screw.

chapters.title: Copy Everything
chapters.summary: Night operation: they photograph and duplicate the ledger, hiding copies with sympathetic dockworkers. Beat: hope with trembling hands.

chapters.title: Alarm
chapters.summary: A guard recognizes Ilya; sirens; Sefa creates a diversion with the boat, getting shot in the escape. Beat: sacrifice raises the price.

chapters.title: Sefa's Stand
chapters.summary: Sefa, wounded, refuses to leave until the others are clear, holding the dock with a flare gun and fury. Beat: courage as inheritance.

chapters.title: Into the Ice Field
chapters.summary: Fleeing up-glacier as the pass narrows, pursued by Hale's men, they navigate crevasses in whiteout. Beat: survival stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Narrowing
chapters.summary: The calving window closes early; Hale's men close in behind; ahead, only a collapsing ice bridge. Beat: trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: Hale on the Ice
chapters.summary: Hale catches them at the bridge, offering Ada the deal one final time. She refuses aloud, naming her brother's crew. Beat: climax of conscience.

chapters.title: The Bridge Breaks
chapters.summary: In the chaos, the ice bridge collapses; Hale falls; Ada saves Ilya at the last second; the pursuers are cut off. Beat: cathartic, costly climax.

chapters.title: Aftermath on the Moraine
chapters.summary: Exhausted, they bury what they can't carry; Ada tends Ilya's frostbite; Sefa's wound is worse than admitted. Beat: grief and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: They descend as the monsoon breaks, carrying duplicate ledgers toward the coastal press and magistrate who once owed Toma. Beat: determined descent.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: The ledger goes public; arrests ripple upstream; Ada testifies against her own former employers, surrendering her badge. Beat: justice outside the law achieved.

chapters.title: What the Debt Was For
chapters.summary: At her brother's grave, Ada reads the recovered manifest aloud, finally saying his crew's names. Beat: mourning completed, debt discharged.

chapters.title: Pardon, Refused
chapters.summary: The Consortium's remnant offers Ada reinstatement and silence money; she declines publicly. Beat: clean refusal, identity claimed.

chapters.title: The Compass Repaired
chapters.summary: Ilya fixes her broken compass before departing to return the original ledger to the valley families; they part without promises but with truth. Beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Summit
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ada's POV: named ranger of a free valley, she climbs to the summit pass each calving season, watching the glacier open the road for whoever comes next. Beat: peace earned, horizon open.
